summary.tldr: Implements budget tax changes, creates a vaping product tax, and adds a new tax on certain luxury vehicles, aircraft and boats.
what_it_does: Creates a labour mobility deduction of up to $4,000 for eligible tradespeople who temporarily relocate for work, starting in the 2022 tax year.

Changes tax rules for passenger vehicles, social assistance amounts, the disability tax credit for type 1 diabetes, the climate action incentive, and zero-emission technology manufacturing, including a new corporate deduction with phased rates.

Treats some social assistance from Canada, a province, or an Indigenous governing body as not blocking parent or dependant status, and adds Indigenous governing bodies to the Children’s Special Allowances Act, all effective January 1, 2020.

Changes charity rules by defining qualifying disbursements, allowing gifts to grantee organizations, limiting gifts to qualified donees to 50% of a charitable organization’s income, and changing disbursement quota and penalty rules.

Treats certain home purchase agreement assignments as taxable real property sales, updates GST/HST rebate rules for nurse practitioners, and creates a federal vaping product tax and licence regime with stamps, duties, warehousing rules, and offences.

Enacts the Select Luxury Items Tax Act for certain vehicles, aircraft and vessels over $100,000 or $250,000, and adds rules for bankruptcy, amalgamations, partnerships, electronic filing and payment, audits, penalties, and offences.
who_it_affects: Buyers of luxury vehicles, aircraft and vessels
summary.background: The bill implements certain provisions of the federal budget tabled on April 7, 2022. It also adds other tax and excise measures, including a new luxury items tax and vaping rules.
